subject: Re: MedCore BYO/KMS + retention window — workback & exceptions
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@medcore.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medcore.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: BYO/KMS + short-term retention extension — initial ask

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team dug into the onboarding checklist and flagged two items we need clarified before we can proceed:

1) BYO/KMS — we need a clear path to hold keys in our HSM (FIPS 140-2) and a description of any early-life key material that Redwood would access during deployment. Is there a supported escrow or temporary key flow for initial seeding?

2) Retention — our data retention policy requires a 90-day ephemeral window for prompt/response logs, but for a short pilot we need to hold a 6-month slice for supervised evaluation. Can you support a temporary retention exception and how that will be audited (exportable logs / attestations)?

Attached: MedCore_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx and a short PO request for the retention exception (medcore_retention_po_request.pdf).

We'd like to get this triaged this week—can you advise next steps and who from your side will own evidence and timelines?

Best,
Aisha Khan
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager
MedCore Health

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: MedCore BYO/KMS & retention — triage notes

Folks — quick internal notes after a quick look through Aisha's questionnaire and attachments:

1) BYOK / HSM:
- We support customer-managed keys with AWS KMS imports and our Private deployment has an HSM integration path. For FIPS HSMs that require manual provisioning, we typically do a one-time manual seed (customer uploads wrapped key or we coordinate a secure transfer) and then we rotate away from that initial material on first successful deployment. That initial seeding is the thing MedCore is asking about.
- Action: Karthik, confirm if we can commit to a documented manual seeding runbook (no Redwood access to unwrapped private keys) and whether we can offer an auditable zero-trust handshake (signed provisioning transcript).

2) Retention exception (6 months temporary):
- We can support a time-bound retention override per-customer at the storage layer for Private/Dedicated. Hosted customers can get an export snapshot + attestation, but we don't normally keep extended logs on hosted seats.
- Evidence options: exportable audit log (S3 export link + MD5), signed attestations from our Security team, and optional transcript demonstrating TTL change.
- Action: Marcus, can you estimate effort to enable a one-off 6-month retention flag and produce export automation? Also we need to note cost and that any extended retention carries higher retention-risk SLA.

3) Sequence & handoffs:
- Dylan to confirm HSM vendor + whether private key material must never leave MedCore.
- Karthik to own BYOK runbook and seeding options.
- Marcus to own retention flag/backfill and export automation.
- Grace to compile evidence pack and proposed language for contract amendment/PO.

I'll draft the evidence checklist and a runbook skeleton by EOD tomorrow. If anyone thinks we should involve Legal or Compliance now, flag it — otherwise we'll keep this as a security triage until we need contract language.

Grace O'Connor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@medcore.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medcore.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO/KMS + short-term retention extension — workback & exceptions

Thanks for the quick responses and the run-of-play. To answer your questions:
- HSM vendor: Thales Luna SA (certificate-based module). MedCore requires that private key material never leaves our controlled environment — we can provide wrapped key blobs and an attestation of the KMS configuration.
- The retention exception is a true temporary need for 6 months only; procurement is ok with an exception PO if you provide an export/attestation flow we can rely on.

Would it help for MedCore to schedule a short vendor call with Thales/our infra folks if the seed process requires vendor coordination? We can do that later this week.

Next steps requested on your side:
1) Confirm whether Redwood can accept a wrapped key blob and perform manual provisioning without ever holding the unwrapped private key.
2) Provide a short statement of what audit exports and attestations Redwood can deliver (example: S3 export URL + signed manifest, ISO timestamps, and Security team's attestation).

If you can send the answers and the SEC-4287 runbook by EOD Friday we'll be in good shape to issue the PO.

Best,
Aisha
